alignments.note: Rule 61: the preposition governing the articular infinitive takes the English clause-introducer 'that'.
Rule 61: the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive has no English realization.
One-token unit takes the whole negation 'no longer', headed on the negative word.
Rules 9, 15 and 74: the supplied subject of the infinitive and the modal auxiliary ride with the infinitive, headed on the lexical verb.
Rules 19 and 57: the article preceding its head noun takes the English determiner.

Rule 58: an article is present and takes 'the', so the attributive adjective stands bare, as tas loipas ekklesias -> 'the rest of the churches' leaves loipas bare at 2CO.12.13. The partitive 'of' rides with the noun it introduces.

Rules 15, 21 and 51: the partitive 'of' and the supplied possessive ride with the noun they determine, discontinuously across the adjective, as at 2CO.12.13 and 2PE.1.20. No genitive pronoun is present and the article is already spent on 'the', so the possessive is an ordinary helper on the noun; marking it 'added' as EPH.6.5 does remains defensible.
Rule 51: the Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is a helper on the noun.
Rules 21 and 51: the dative's case preposition and the supplied determiner ride with the anarthrous noun.
Rule 17: a source noun rendered by 'of + noun' heads on the noun.
Rules 21 and 51: the case preposition and supplied determiner ride with the anarthrous noun.
Rule 17: 'of God' heads on the noun.
